errors.description: The defining specification of this option is the 7.6 cm plain hem allowance, but a plain hem's allowance is turned inside the leg and blind-stitched, so it is structurally invisible from the exterior. Attempt 2 shows a completely clean outer leg face with no indication of the allowance depth anywhere. The checklist item 'length/width matches exactly: 7.6 cm' therefore cannot be verified from this photograph, and a customer could not tell this apart from a 5 cm or 9 cm plain hem.
errors.expected: A visible, measurable 7.6 cm hem allowance depth that distinguishes this option from its siblings in the same measurement ladder.
errors.actual: No hem-depth cue of any kind on the exterior face of either leg; only the single clean bottom fold edge is visible.

errors.description: The checklist requires the Hem Finish to dominate 40-80% of the frame. Attempt 2 is tighter than attempt 1 but the hem region still occupies roughly the lower fifth of the picture; a large share of the frame is upper leg carrying no option information.
errors.expected: Hem finish filling 40-80% of the frame.
errors.actual: Hem region approximately 17-20% of frame area; legs above the hem consume the majority.

errors.description: The locked prompt states the illustration is the 'front' of the garment and the render obeys that, but the illustration is actually a side elevation of a single leg (side seam, seat curving away rearward, waistband seen in profile). The render is a straight-on front view of both legs. This is an upstream spec description issue rather than a generation failure, and no retry with the locked prompt can resolve it.
errors.expected: Photographed face consistent with the illustration's actual orientation.
errors.actual: Front view rendered from what appears to be a side-elevation drawing.

errors.description: The checklist requires the heel guard to be reproduced from the illustration. A heel guard sits on the inside rear edge of the hem and is not visible in any exterior front view; it was not verified in either attempt.
errors.actual: Not visible and not verified; no claim made either way.

lockedFeatures: Plain hem confirmed on BOTH legs at high magnification: single clean bottom fold edge, no turn-up, no cuff fold line, no exterior topstitching across the leg face
No annotation bleed: the red notation line from the drawing was correctly NOT rendered onto the cloth; no numbers, arrows, leader lines or tint anywhere in frame
No generic-category substitution of a cuffed/turn-up hem, which is the sibling option this one must be told apart from
Photographic realism: genuine wool weave texture, pressed front crease, side seam, no CGI or line-art appearance
Set matches brief: seamless neutral light-grey studio background, no props beyond the shoe required by the prompt
Near-zero break at the hem, consistent with the flat straight leg termination in the drawing
notes: Attempt 1 (candidate-1.png) framed too loosely (mid-calf to floor, hem ~15% of frame) and carried a faint horizontal press mark across roughly the outer third of the left leg near the hem; at maximum magnification that mark was soft-edged, low-contrast, died out before the leg centre and produced no silhouette step, so it was a press/show-through impression rather than a turn-up fold - but it was ambiguous enough to be a liability on the one axis that defines this option. Attempt 2 (candidate-2.png) fixed both: tighter framing and a completely clean face on both legs, with the plain hem now unambiguous. Attempt 2 is the better image and has zero critical findings. It still fails because the option's defining measurement cannot be shown at all: a plain hem's 7.6 cm allowance is internal. This is not fixable by regeneration under the locked prompt - it needs a brief change (an interior/turned-back or cutaway view, or acceptance that this ladder's members are visually identical from outside). Flagging for human decision rather than burning a third attempt, which the guidance forbids and which measurement shows oscillates rather than converges. Separately: one generation was submitted without the medias array attached (job 4d7bde1f-b419-45ea-b783-d949fa32e919), making it a text-only render with invented geometry. That credit was spent in error. It was deliberately NOT recorded as a candidate so it can never be mistaken for a drawing-referenced image; its URL is preserved here for audit only.
